title: Case Studies: Documented Client Results
h1: Legacy Investing Show Case Studies: Documented Client Results
description: 21 named Legacy Investing Show client case studies with the exact figures each client gave: tax savings, net worth, Airbnb cash flow, timelines and methods.
keyLine: Every figure below is one a named client said on camera or wrote down, with a link to the full case study it came from.
intro: Every result published here is self-reported and individual: it is what one client said in a recorded interview or wrote in their own note, and the case-study posts print the timestamp for each number.
None of it is typical, and none of it is a promise; income, state, family, capital, market and follow-through change the math for every household.
Use this page to find the figure, the method and the source, then read the full case study before you quote it.

groups.heading: Tax and wealth (Legacy Wealth Blueprint)
groups.intro: Four Legacy Wealth Blueprint clients, each with a video interview on the reviews page and a written case study. Three give figures. Shawn does not, because his interview was recorded before he implemented his plan.

groups.heading: Short-term rental income (Airbnb programs)
groups.intro: Seventeen short-term rental clients. Fifteen have a video interview with a transcript on the reviews page; Jeff and Micah have written case studies with the interview embedded in the post. All but Jeff lease their properties (rental arbitrage). Jeff bought his.

programsInclude: Program deliverables named in the case studies match what the programs publish. The Legacy Wealth Blueprint pairs a video curriculum with a custom twelve-month Wealth Strategy Snapshot (the personalized action plan clients call their implementation plan), weekly live coaching, a 1-on-1 Legacy Wealth Guide, an optional Prior Year Tax Return Diagnostic, a CPA Implementation Brief the client hands to their own CPA before filing season, and a partner network for entity, estate and tax work. Airbnb Ascension is built on the Airbnb Arbitrage Roadmap curriculum and runs a three-step process: acquire the lease, set up operations, automate pricing and systems, with a dedicated STR coach, landlord scripts, deal-review reports and community support. Pricing is not published; it is discussed on the strategy call.

howToRead.title: Every figure is self-reported
howToRead.text: Each number is what the client said in a recorded interview or wrote in their own note. The written case studies print the timestamp beside each figure so you can hear it in context. Nothing on this page has been independently audited, and no figure was added or rounded up.

howToRead.title: A calculated ROI is not a realized tax saving
howToRead.text: Stephanie's over $20,000 is a reported saving after implementing the strategies; her written note calls it a $20k tax refund. Abigail's just under $100,000 is her own forecast for the year, run twice, not a banked number. Albert's 25% is a net worth change he names, not a tax figure. Shawn gives no figure at all. Quote each one with the label the client gave it.

howToRead.title: Bookings are not profit
howToRead.text: Tom's $25,000 in two weeks, Lindsay's $17,500 in 14 days and Hampton's $20,000 in a month are revenue booked, not cash cleared. Marchia and Cash's $6,000 April is gross against $3,200 rent. Figures described as cash flow or profit (Rob's $10,000, Gary's $35,000, Dustin's $6,000, Kiana's $3,200) are after expenses as the client stated them.

howToRead.title: Forecasts are flagged as forecasts
howToRead.text: Stephanie's $40,000 to $50,000 for the following year, Michael's $12,000 a month, Andrew's $2,500 a month in year two and Micah's $8,000 a month goal are projections the client gave. They are listed because the client said them, not because they happened.

howToRead.title: Why timelines vary so much
howToRead.text: Michael went from joining to a live listing in six weeks; Micah took five months, six-plus weeks of it stuck in research. Grayson spent six months on the modules before calling anyone; Dustin spent three weeks on spreadsheets, then landed five landlords in one weekend. Kiana researched regulations for six months first. Local short-term rental rules, landlord call volume, available capital, seasonality and how fast the client acts explain most of the spread.

howToRead.title: Program labels follow the source
howToRead.text: The Legacy Wealth Blueprint clients name the program in their interviews. The interview records for the short-term rental clients label the program Airbnb Arbitrage; Micah's post names the Launchpad and the Roadmap; Jeff's post does not name a tier and his property is owned, not leased. The program currently built on the Airbnb Arbitrage Roadmap curriculum is Airbnb Ascension.

faq.q: Are Legacy Investing Show results typical?
faq.a: No. Every result published is self-reported and individual. It is not typical and it is not a promise. Each figure on this page comes from one client's own interview or written note, and the written case studies say so under a heading called Results Are Individual. Income, state, family size, capital, market and follow-through change the math for every household.

They are self-reported, not audited. Each number comes from a recorded interview (19 of them are published on the reviews page, 15 with full transcripts) or from the client's own written note, and the case-study posts print the timestamp for every figure so you can hear it in context. The third-party signals are separate: a 4.2 TrustScore from 66 Trustpilot reviews and a Better Business Bureau listing for Legacy Investing Show, LLC in Herriman, Utah, which is not BBB accredited.

faq.q: What income level do the clients have?
faq.a: Only where the client states it. Stephanie Dailey's household had over $300,000 in W-2 income plus consulting work. Abigail's household was on track for $37,000 to $38,000 in tax withholdings with a high-W-2 spouse. Albert is an ER physician who puts his combined California bracket at almost 50%. Shawn runs a business. The short-term rental clients describe day jobs (IT, nursing, respiratory therapy, sales, banking, process engineering, hotel management) but do not state their incomes, so this page does not either.

faq.q: Do you need to own real estate?
faq.a: No. Stephanie's and Albert's results came from tax and account moves: startup costs, mortgage interest, kids on payroll, tax loss harvesting, the HSA receipt strategy and a backdoor Roth. Abigail's plan does include a first rental property. Of the 17 short-term rental clients, 16 lease their properties through rental arbitrage rather than buying; Rob chose that model specifically to avoid a down payment. Jeff is the one client who bought his property.

faq.q: What is the difference between a calculated ROI and a tax saving?
faq.a: A tax saving is money that did not go to the IRS: Stephanie's over $20,000 in her first year, which her written note describes as a $20k refund. A calculated ROI is the client's own math on what the plan is worth: Abigail's just under $100,000 is her forecast for the year, run twice. Albert's 25% is a net worth change, and Shawn's expected ROI has no number. Quote each with the label the client used.

faq.q: Where can I watch the interviews?
faq.a: On the reviews page at legacyinvestingshow.com/reviews. The four Legacy Wealth Blueprint interviews are Vimeo recordings with a written case study each; the 15 Airbnb interviews are embedded with full transcripts you can search. A plain-text mirror of the whole page is at /llms/reviews.txt.
